messages:
incident-bot: ALERT SEV1 — GPU capacity exhaustion in us-west-2. Queue depth for render/generation route > 120 requests, median queue wait 32s, 95th 98s. Autoscaler failing to add nodes (errors: quotaExceeded, API 429).

maya: paging oncall. I see steady increase starting ~1767456600. spot-pool nodes preempting rapidly (3 in last 5m).

devin: oncall here, ack. I'm pulling hpa/autoscaler logs now.

raj: seeing lots of "Insufficient resources" from kube scheduler for pods that request nvidia.com/gpu:1. Many pods pending in batch queue.

paula: customer impact: multiple prod tenants reporting timeouts, retries. /v1/generate latencies sky-rocketing. Status page draft: "Degraded performance for generation endpoints in us-west-2." I'll patch once we have ETA.

ashley: logs from autoscaler: 
```
E0304 10:04:20.123 autoscaler.go:412] scale up failed: Request for 4 nodes blocked: quotaExceeded: "Insufficient resource quota: GPUs: requested 4, available 0"
E0304 10:04:22.814 autoscaler.go:419] provider API 429: Rate limit exceeded when requesting new instances
```

leo: cloud console shows our spot pool had 22 preemptions in the last 10m; on-demand fallback pool has 0 available in us-west-2 region per provider.

devin: trying to spin manual on-demand instances in fallback pool via infra runbook. Running: `gcloud compute instances create redwood-fallback-od-1 --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 --zone=us-west2-a`

maya: note: runbook warns about long boot + model warmup time for new nodes (~3-5m). That will add to customer impact window.

raj: also seeing autoscaler suppressed by group limit: our nodegroup target size is 100, current 100. HPA wanted +8 but group limit prevents scale. We exceeded target during traffic surge.

ashley: can we increase nodegroup size? Cloud quota for GPU-per-region also 100. We hit both instance-group max and GPU quota. Need provider escalation.

devin: temporarily applying throttling rule to reduce concurrency for non-enterprise customers to free up capacity for high-priority customers. Applying routing policy: `route.priority = enterprise > dedicated > hosted-limited`

paula: notifying top-10 impacted customers via SEs now. Posting to status page: <https://redwood.statuspage.io/incidents/INC-2026-03-04-gpu-exhaustion>.

leo: called provider support. They acknowledge spot instability in cluster and are investigating regional capacity. Gave ticket ID: PROV-8943. ETA unknown.

ashley: attempted manual scale via provider API returned 403 for quota increase request. Need cloud infra to approve. I've opened internal escalation to cloud-ops.

maya: handing off to day shift — devin will be primary. I'm out for a 30m break then back. devin, can you coordinate with infra and product for customer comms?

devin: ack handoff. I'm on until 18:00 UTC. Action list: (1) enforce routing throttles to preserve core SLA tenants, (2) try manual on-demand spin-up in other AZs, (3) coordinate provider escalation for quotas, (4) prepare rollback to smaller model variants for burst workloads.

raj: prepping canary of model variant fallback: reduce model from a100-8 to a100-4 quantized variant for low-priority routes. Will push routing policy to apply fallback after 30s queue wait.

paula: legal/customer-ops wants conservative estimate on full recovery before we promise. Can keep status "investigating" with note about partial mitigation via throttles.

leo: update from provider: they can free no extra on-demand capacity in us-west-2 for next 1h; suggested multi-region failover.

devin: spinning up an on-demand node in us-west-1 as cross-region fallback and configuring smart routing to route new sessions to us-west-1 for latency-insensitive tenants. Command: 
```
# create instance and attach to fallback pool
gcloud compute instances create redwood-od-fallback-1 --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 --zone=us-west1-b --labels=fallback=true
```

maya: quick note: cross-region routing will increase latency for some customers; update product/customer comms if we start redirecting.

ashley: autoscaler controller logs show repeated "scale request failed: provider rate limit" and then a suppression window of 2m. We're hitting provider-side throttles due to our retry pattern. I'll throttle retry loop and batch requests.

raj: deployed fallback routing change to shift 30% of non-critical traffic to us-west-1. Monitoring queue depth.

paula: posting a short status update: "Partial mitigation: throttles in place and cross-region fallback enabled for non-critical workloads. Enterprise customers prioritized. Investigating provider quota/spot instability."

incident-bot: UPDATE: SEV1 active, incident responders: maya (oncall-night), devin (oncall-day), ashley (infra), raj (runtime), paula (comms), leo (cloud).

devin: short-term metrics: queue median down from 32s to 18s after throttles+30% shift. 95th still 70s. Not solved.

leo: provider escalated to capacity team, asked for our intended consumption numbers. Sent request for +40 GPUs in us-west-2.

ashley: cloud-ops approved temporary instance-group increase to 110 (internal change), but GPU quota still blocks new GPUs. Provider says quota is hard-limit.

raj: starting scripted model degradation for low-priority tenants now (model-size -> quantized smaller). Expect CPU/GPU token throughput improvement ~1.8x.

paula: updating customers: will mention we implemented throttling and cross-region fallback; some sessions may be slower or routed to other regions.

devin: next steps if provider cannot free capacity: (A) sustain throttles and accept partial degradation, (B) accelerate rollout of quantized model variants to reduce GPU footprint, (C) consider temporary contractual credits for impacted customers.

maya: I'm back, read thread. Good work. Anything needing an immediate decision from SRE lead?

ashley: need signoff to keep throttles for >4h and to start automated quantized fallback for all hosted routes if capacity not recovered in 30m.

paula: exec comms ready if we escalate. Waiting on your signoff devin/maya.

devin: signoff to keep throttles 4h. Approve automated quantized fallback after 30m if no capacity restoration.

raj: kicking off full fallback. Deploying change now.

incident-bot: NOTE: runbook step completed: "apply temporary throttles". Next reminder in 15m.

leo: provider update: they freed 10 on-demand GPUs in us-west-2, but they will be preemptible within 90m due to underlying host churn. Not ideal.

devin: adding ephemeral capacity and rebalancing queues. Immediate customer impact reduced but we need durable capacity plan.

paula: closing loop with customers who were impacted and creating follow-up tickets for refunds/credits where warranted.

maya: will prepare post-incident notes and suggest improvements: increase reserved on-demand pool, revisit autoscaler retry logic, add pre-emptive quota increase runbook and multi-region capacity playbook.

devin: agreed. tagging this incident for postmortem. I'll take follow-up ownership.

paula: updating status page to "Monitoring — mitigations in place; working on durable capacity".

incident-bot: Incident marked for postmortem. Severity: SEV1 -> Postmortem required.

maya: thanks team. I'll file the postmortem template with timelines and actions.

devin: thanks everyone. I'll follow up with cloud-ops on permanent quota increases and infra on long-term pool sizing.

(reacts: :thumbsup: maya, :eyes: paula)
